proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\delta>0\).  Spectral clipping gives the deterministic bounds
\[
 \lambda_{\max}(\widehat V_{j,n})\le2\overline\omega,
 \qquad
 Q_{j,n}\ge\frac n{2\overline\omega}
                 \|\widehat s_{j,n}\|_2^2.
\tag{32}
\]
There is a finite constant \(C_{\alpha,J,q}\), depending only on \(\alpha\), \(J\), and \(q\), such that \(\widehat c_n\le C_{\alpha,J,q}\) on every sample.  Indeed, under the Gaussian law defining \(\widehat c_n\), every standardized label block has the \(N(0,I_{q+1})\) distribution.  Therefore the union bound gives
\[
 \Pr\left\{
  \max_{j\in\mathcal J}
  \|(E_j\widetilde\Omega_nE_j^{\top})^{-1/2}E_jZ\|_2>x
 \right\}
 \le J\Pr\{\|N(0,I_{q+1})\|_2>x\},
\]
and the right-hand side is smaller than \(\alpha\) for all sufficiently large fixed \(x\).

Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:joint\text{-}gaussian}\) and the upper eigenvalue bound on \(\Omega_n\) imply
\[
 \lim_{M\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}
 \sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M}
 \Pr_{\mathbb P_n}\!\left\{
 \|\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n)\|_2>M
 \right\}=0.
\tag{33}
\]
For \(\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M(\delta)\) and \(j\notin\mathcal C_n\), the definition of fixed separation gives \(\|s_{j,n}\|_2\ge\delta\).  On the event
\(
 \|\widehat s_{j,n}-s_{j,n}\|_2<\delta/2
\), equation (32) yields
\[
 Q_{j,n}\ge\frac{n\delta^2}{8\overline\omega}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), this exceeds \(C_{\alpha,J,q}^2\), and Definition \(\mathrm{def:profile\text{-}intervals}\) then makes the profile empty.  A union bound over the fixed label set and (33) prove
\[
 \sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M(\delta)}
 \Pr_{\mathbb P_n}\{\exists j\in\mathcal J\setminus\mathcal C_n:
 I_{j,n}(\alpha)\ne\varnothing\}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{34}
\]

It remains to bound the close-label profiles.  The clipped covariance and its principal blocks satisfy, on every sample,
\[
 \|\widehat V_{j,n}^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\frac2{\underline\omega},
 \quad
 \|\widehat u_{j,n}\|_2\le2\overline\omega,
 \quad
 \|\widehat\gamma_{j,n}\|_2
 \le G:=\frac{4\overline\omega}{\underline\omega},
 \quad
 0<\widehat\sigma_{j,n}^2\le2\overline\omega.
\tag{35}
\]
Strict positivity of the Schur complement follows from positive definiteness of the label block.  For \(j\in\mathcal C_n\), Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:exact\text{-}score\text{-}transport}\) gives \(s_{j,n}=0\) and \(b_{j,n}=\tau_n\).  Hence the center
\(
 \widehat b_{j,n}-\widehat\gamma_{j,n}^{\top}\widehat s_{j,n}
\)
satisfies
\[
 \sqrt n\left|
 \widehat b_{j,n}-\widehat\gamma_{j,n}^{\top}\widehat s_{j,n}-\tau_n
 \right|
 \le(1+G)\|E_j\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n)\|_2.
\tag{36}
\]
Whenever its profile is nonempty, its half-length is at most
\[
 n^{-1/2}\widehat\sigma_{j,n}\widehat c_n
 \le n^{-1/2}\sqrt{2\overline\omega}\,C_{\alpha,J,q}.
\tag{37}
\]
On the event in (34) that every false-label profile is empty, every point of the projected hull lies within
\[
 n^{-1/2}\left\{
 (1+G)\|\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n)\|_2
 +\sqrt{2\overline\omega}\,C_{\alpha,J,q}
 \right\}
\]
of \(\tau_n\), by (36)--(37) and convexity.  If the hull is empty its declared diameter is zero; otherwise its diameter is at most twice this radius.  Combining this bound with (33)--(34), and then sending \(\xi\to\infty\), proves
\[
 \lim_{\xi\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}
 \sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M(\delta)}
 \Pr_{\mathbb P_n}\{\sqrt n\operatorname{diam}
 (C_n^{\mathrm{proj}}(\alpha))>\xi\}=0.
\]
Together with (34), this is exactly the two-part claim.  Notice that the proof establishes root-\(n\) tightness only: the unchanged maximum critical value still ranges over all \(J\) labels, so this theorem by itself does not assert the ordinary one-label first-order constant.

added_lemmas.statement:
For the split and sequences in Definition \(\mathrm{def:pilot\text{-}adaptive\text{-}hull}\), the pilot and main statistics are independent.  There exist \(n_0\in\mathbb N\) and \(K<\infty\) such that
\[
 \sup_{n\ge n_0}\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_n}\!\left[
 \left\|\sqrt{m_n}(\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm P}-\theta_n)\right\|_2^2
 \right]\le K.
\]
\[
 \sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M}
 d_{\mathrm{Pr}}\!\left(
 \mathcal L_{\mathbb P_n}(\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm M}-\theta_n)),
 N(0,\Omega_n)
 \right)\longrightarrow0,
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M}
 \Pr_{\mathbb P_n}\!\left\{
 \left\|\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm M}-\widehat\theta_n)\right\|_2>\varepsilon
 \right\}\longrightarrow0
 \quad\text{for every }\varepsilon>0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_n}\!\left[
 \min\{1,\|\widetilde\Omega_n^{\mathrm M}-\Omega_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\}
 \right]\longrightarrow0,
\]
and every eigenvalue of \(\widetilde\Omega_n^{\mathrm M}\) belongs to \([\underline\omega/2,2\overline\omega]\).
added_lemmas.justification: The independent screen and the untouched main-sample calibration require a joint uniform approximation with the pilot's smaller rate exposed explicitly.
added_lemmas.gap: The frozen Gaussian lemma concerns the full sample and does not itself state that deletion of an \(o(n)\) pilot preserves the root-\(n\) law and covariance estimate.
added_lemmas.consumer: The two pilot-adaptive theorems use this lemma for selection independence, score-screen concentration, and feasible main-sample Gaussian calibration.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the independent-pilot construction satisfies
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M}
 \Pr_{\mathbb P_n}\{\tau_n\in C_n^{\mathrm{ad}}(\alpha)\}
 \ge1-\alpha.
\]
This conclusion is uniform over all exact-close arrays, including root-\(n\)-local separations and multiple-close-donor faces, and its covariance calibration retains every shared treated-group and reused-control covariance encoded by \(A\).
added_lemmas.justification: Pilot screening is useful only if it preserves honesty at local label collisions and on faces with several exact donors.
added_lemmas.gap: Ordinary consistent model selection does not justify a confidence set uniformly over root-\(n\)-local score separations; independence and simultaneous main-sample calibration are both needed.
added_lemmas.consumer: Applications may reduce the calibration menu using prespecified sample splitting without sacrificing the conditional uniform coverage guarantee.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every fixed \(\delta>0\), the pilot screen consistently recovers the entire close set:
\[
 \sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M(\delta)}
 \Pr_{\mathbb P_n}\{\widehat{\mathcal S}_n\ne\mathcal C_n\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
If \(\mathcal C_n=\{j_n\}\), define the ordinary full-sample, known-label residual-effect Wald interval
\[
 W_{j_n,n}^{\mathrm{ord}}(\alpha)
 =\left[
 r_{j_n}(\widetilde\Omega_n)\widehat\theta_n
 \mathbin{\pm}n^{-1/2}\sigma_{j_n}(\widetilde\Omega_n)
 \Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)
 \right].
\]
Then, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \sup_{\substack{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M(\delta):\\
                   \mathcal C_n=\{j_n\}}}
 \Pr_{\mathbb P_n}\!\left\{
 \sqrt n\max\left(
  \left|\inf C_n^{\mathrm{ad}}(\alpha)-\inf W_{j_n,n}^{\mathrm{ord}}(\alpha)\right|,
  \left|\sup C_n^{\mathrm{ad}}(\alpha)-\sup W_{j_n,n}^{\mathrm{ord}}(\alpha)\right|
 \right)>\varepsilon
 \right\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus the adaptive hull has the ordinary single-label Wald center, variance, and critical constant to first order when the exact close label is unique; for several close labels it calibrates only over that recovered face.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For \(j\in\mathcal C_n\), the argument in (21), followed by a union bound over the fixed set \(\mathcal J\), gives
\[
 \sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M(\delta)}
 \Pr_{\mathbb P_n}\{\mathcal C_n\nsubseteq S_n^0\}
 \le \frac{JK}{a_n^2}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{25}
\]
For \(j\notin\mathcal C_n\), fixed separation gives \(\|s_{j,n}\|_2\ge\delta\).  If that label belongs to the raw screen, the reverse triangle inequality implies
\[
 \sqrt{m_n}\|\widehat s_{j,n}^{\mathrm P}-s_{j,n}\|_2
 \ge \sqrt{m_n}\delta-a_n.
\]
The pilot second-moment bound and Markov's inequality therefore give, once the positive denominator is defined,
\[
 \sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathfrak M(\delta)}
 \Pr_{\mathbb P_n}\{j\in S_n^0\}
 \le \frac K{(\sqrt{m_n}\delta-a_n)^2}\longrightarrow0,
\tag{26}
\]
because \(a_n/\sqrt{m_n}\to0\).  Equations (25)--(26) and a union bound show \(S_n^0=\mathcal C_n\) with probability tending to one uniformly.  On this event the raw screen is nonempty by Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:nonempty\text{-}close\text{-}set}\), so the fallback is inactive and \(\widehat{\mathcal S}_n=\mathcal C_n\).  This proves recovery.

Now suppose \(\mathcal C_n=\{j_n\}\).  On the recovery event, the maximum in the definition of \(k_{1-\alpha}\) contains one standardized nondegenerate normal coordinate.  Hence, exactly and for every positive definite covariance matrix,
\[
 k_{1-\alpha}(\{j_n\},\Omega)=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2).
\tag{27}
\]
Definitions and (27) show that on this event \(C_n^{\mathrm{ad}}(\alpha)\) equals the main-sample ordinary interval
\[
 W_{j_n,n}^{\mathrm M}(\alpha)
 =\left[
 r_{j_n}(\widetilde\Omega_n^{\mathrm M})\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm M}
 \mathbin{\pm}n^{-1/2}\sigma_{j_n}(\widetilde\Omega_n^{\mathrm M})
 \Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)
 \right].
\tag{28}
\]

It remains to compare (28) with the full-sample interval.  Lemmas \(\mathrm{lem:spectral\text{-}clipping\text{-}negligible}\) and \(\mathrm{lem:pilot\text{-}main\text{-}split}\) give
\[
 \|\widetilde\Omega_n^{\mathrm M}-\widetilde\Omega_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1),
 \qquad
 \sqrt n\|\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm M}-\widehat\theta_n\|_2
 =o_{\mathbb P_n}(1)
\tag{29}
\]
uniformly.  Continuity on the clipped compact covariance set turns the first relation into
\[
 r_{j_n}(\widetilde\Omega_n^{\mathrm M})-r_{j_n}(\widetilde\Omega_n)
 =o_{\mathbb P_n}(1),
 \qquad
 \sigma_{j_n}(\widetilde\Omega_n^{\mathrm M})-sigma_{j_n}(\widetilde\Omega_n)
 =o_{\mathbb P_n}(1).
\tag{30}
\]
Because \(j_n\) is close, Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:exact\text{-}score\text{-}transport}\) gives \(s_{j_n,n}=0\) and \(b_{j_n,n}=\tau_n\).  Hence, for either estimated covariance \(\Omega'\), the definition of the residual row gives
\[
 r_{j_n}(\Omega')\theta_n
 =b_{j_n,n}-u_{j_n}(\Omega')^{\top}V_{j_n}(\Omega')^{-1}s_{j_n,n}
 =\tau_n.
\]
Thus the potentially unbounded level of \(\theta_n\) cancels, and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sqrt n\left\{
 r_{j_n}(\widetilde\Omega_n^{\mathrm M})\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm M}
 -r_{j_n}(\widetilde\Omega_n)\widehat\theta_n
 \right\}\\
 &\quad=
 r_{j_n}(\widetilde\Omega_n^{\mathrm M})
 \sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm M}-\widehat\theta_n)
 +\{r_{j_n}(\widetilde\Omega_n^{\mathrm M})
      -r_{j_n}(\widetilde\Omega_n)\}
 \sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n)
 =o_{\mathbb P_n}(1).
\end{aligned}
\tag{31}
\]
Here the last factor is uniformly tight by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:joint\text{-}gaussian}\), while all residual rows are uniformly bounded by covariance regularity.  Equations (30)--(31) show that both endpoints of (28) differ from the corresponding endpoints of \(W_{j_n,n}^{\mathrm{ord}}(\alpha)\) by \(o_{\mathbb P_n}(n^{-1/2})\), uniformly.  Combining this fact with recovery proves the displayed endpoint equivalence.  The final multiple-face assertion follows from the already-proved recovery \(\widehat{\mathcal S}_n=\mathcal C_n\).
added_lemmas.justification: The vanishing pilot removes false labels under fixed separation while costing only \(o(n)\) observations, so the unique-label procedure can recover the ordinary first-order constant.
added_lemmas.gap: The original projected hull is root-\(n\) tight but retains a critical value maximized over all \(J\) labels and therefore is not first-order oracle-equivalent.
added_lemmas.consumer: With one separated exact donor, the adaptive confidence set has the same endpoints to order \(o_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2})\) as the ordinary known-label residual-effect Wald interval.

proposed.name: Independent-pilot adaptive residual-effect hull
proposed.construction:
Fix deterministic sequences \(m_n\in\mathbb N\) and \(a_n>0\) satisfying \(m_n\to\infty\), \(m_n/n\to0\), \(a_n\to\infty\), and \(a_n/\sqrt{m_n}\to0\).  Because \(R\) is fixed and \(n_r/n\to\lambda_r>0\), \(m_n<n_r\) for every \(r\in\mathcal R\) at all sufficiently large indices.  At such an index, use observations \(1,\ldots,m_n\) from every group as the pilot sample and the remaining observations as the main sample, and set
\[
 \widehat\mu_{r,n}^{\mathrm P}
 =m_n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{m_n}W_{ri},
 \qquad
 \widehat\mu_{r,n}^{\mathrm M}
 =(n_r-m_n)^{-1}\sum_{i=m_n+1}^{n_r}W_{ri}.
\]
Stack the group means in the same order as \(\widehat\mu_n\), and define
\[
 \widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm P}=A\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm P},
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm M}=A\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm M}.
\]
Let \(\widehat s_{j,n}^{\mathrm P}\) be the first \(q\) coordinates of \(E_j\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm P}\).  Apply the shared-group covariance formula to the main sample, with divisor \(n_r-m_n\) in each centered within-group covariance and multiplier \(n/(n_r-m_n)\), and apply the same eigenvalue clipping to \([\underline\omega/2,2\overline\omega]\); denote the result by \(\widetilde\Omega_n^{\mathrm M}\).

For every \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\), partition
\[
 E_j\Omega E_j^{\top}
 =\begin{pmatrix}V_j(\Omega)&u_j(\Omega)\\
 u_j(\Omega)^{\top}&v_j(\Omega)\end{pmatrix}
\]
and define the residual-effect row and its standard deviation by
\[
 r_j(\Omega)=\bigl(-u_j(\Omega)^{\top}V_j(\Omega)^{-1},1\bigr)E_j,
 \qquad
 \sigma_j^2(\Omega)=r_j(\Omega)\Omega r_j(\Omega)^{\top}.
\]
Positive definiteness makes \(V_j(\Omega)\) invertible and its Schur complement \(\sigma_j^2(\Omega)\) strictly positive.  For every nonempty \(S\subseteq\mathcal J\), let
\[
 k_{1-\alpha}(S,\Omega)
 =\inf\left\{x\ge0:
 \Pr\left(
   \max_{j\in S}\frac{|r_j(\Omega)Z|}{\sigma_j(\Omega)}\le x
 \right)\ge1-\alpha\right\},
 \qquad Z\sim N(0,\Omega).
\]
Define the raw pilot screen \(S_n^0=\{j\in\mathcal J:\sqrt{m_n}\|\widehat s_{j,n}^{\mathrm P}\|_2\le a_n\}\) and the nonempty retained set
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal S}_n=
 \begin{cases}
 S_n^0,&S_n^0\ne\varnothing,\\
 \mathcal J,&S_n^0=\varnothing.
 \end{cases}
\]
For \(j\in\widehat{\mathcal S}_n\), put
\[
 \widehat t_{j,n}^{\mathrm M}
 =r_j(\widetilde\Omega_n^{\mathrm M})\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm M},
 \qquad
 I_{j,n}^{\mathrm{ad}}(\alpha)
 =\left[
 \widehat t_{j,n}^{\mathrm M}
 \mathbin{\pm}n^{-1/2}\sigma_j(\widetilde\Omega_n^{\mathrm M})
 k_{1-\alpha}(\widehat{\mathcal S}_n,\widetilde\Omega_n^{\mathrm M})
 \right],
\]
and put \(I_{j,n}^{\mathrm{ad}}(\alpha)=\varnothing\) otherwise.  The pilot-adaptive hull is
\[
 C_n^{\mathrm{ad}}(\alpha)
 =\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{j\in\mathcal J}
 I_{j,n}^{\mathrm{ad}}(\alpha)\right).
\]
At the finitely many indices for which some \(m_n\ge n_r\), define \(C_n^{\mathrm{ad}}(\alpha)=C_n^{\mathrm{proj}}(\alpha)\).  This convention has no asymptotic effect.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The existing maximum-critical projection is root-\(n\) tight but retains an all-label first-order critical value; independent screening followed by scalar residual-effect calibration supplies the requested oracle constant.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: The finite-sample confidence outputs are \(C_n^{\mathrm{proj}}(\alpha)\) and the oracle-adaptive \(C_n^{\mathrm{ad}}(\alpha)\). The finite local weak-separation benchmark is the score-only, bounded-effect-spread Gaussian minimax risk of Definition def:score-face-minimax-risk, which observes \(b\) exactly; the unbounded full-vector risk \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)\) is retained only as an infinite-frontier obstruction.

proposed.comparator_claim: Their Proposition 3 recovers conventional inference when one argmax-selected option is chosen with probability tending to one; their selection rule and selected-option estimand differ from an exact-zero donor face.
Their Bayes--minimax result assumes dominated product-measurable laws and fixed sigma-finite expected-measure loss, so it is used only as a template for the unresolved general score-face program.
Simultaneous inference supplies universal post-selection coverage at a possible multiplicity cost.
Weak-identification subsequence arguments motivate uniformity but do not establish Le Cam transfer for the score-only donor-face experiment.
Conditional Gaussian inference motivates identification-strength robustness but does not solve the donor-face expected-diameter problem.
Few-treated-group difference-in-differences inference handles unequal group sizes using many controls rather than many iid micro observations inside fixed labels.
Cross-fitted synthetic-control inference concerns time-series average effects, not exact-zero donor-label uncertainty.
Global deficiency equivalence there uses domination, smoothness, positivity, compactness, and explicit likelihood-process approximation beyond the present fourth-moment panel class.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Comparator positioning must distinguish the new oracle construction from argmax selection and must quarantine unproved decision duality and transfer claims.

prose_updates.tldr: A fixed finite menu of donor stacks is nonregular when validity means exact equality of a noisy pretreatment score. Under the explicit nonempty-close and shared-slope additive untreated-change assumptions, exact score equality transports the donor contrast to the same ATT for every close label. The spectrally clipped projected hull is uniformly honest and root-\(n\) tight under fixed separation, but its all-label critical value is not oracle-equivalent. An independent \(o(n)\) pilot now screens labels, and scalar residual-effect calibration on the untouched sample remains uniformly honest, recovers the exact close face under fixed separation, and has ordinary one-label Wald endpoints when that face is a singleton. The original full-vector Gaussian frontier is infinite and its noisy-effect limit is mis-scaled; the repaired finite frontier observes donor effects exactly, places Gaussian noise only on root-\(n\)-scaled scores, and bounds their spread. Its two-face Mahalanobis subproblem has an exact likelihood-ratio value and zero-diameter elbow, while only the exact general-\(J\) constant and a suitably restricted score-only transfer remain unresolved. Ranked near-balance does not validate the historical CMS estimates.

project_justification.gap: Existing few-treated panel methods, long-time-series synthetic-control methods, and argmax post-selection methods do not give an honest confidence set for an ATT whose admissible label is defined by an exact population-zero score. The original maximum-critical hull also cannot supply an oracle first-order constant merely because false profiles disappear, and a full Gaussian experiment with fixed noise in donor effects has the wrong local scaling.
project_justification.niche: The motivating CMS workflow has finitely many prespecified comparison labels, many iid beneficiary-level observations within each state, unequal group sizes, and covariance from treated or control groups reused across labels. The mathematical class is narrower than the historical workflow: it explicitly requires at least one exact close donor and a shared-slope additive model for untreated changes. Its zero-face selection rule and common-face ATT are neither a special case nor a superclass of argmax selection with a selected-option estimand.
project_justification.fill: The note proves exact-score causal transport, shared-covariance Gaussian inversion, uniform coverage, and fixed-separation root-\(n\) tightness. It adds an independent vanishing-pilot procedure that is uniformly honest and recovers ordinary known-label Wald endpoints for a unique separated close donor. It also replaces the infinite, mis-scaled full-vector frontier by a bounded-spread score-only Gaussian problem, derives the exact two-face Mahalanobis benchmark and a finite simultaneous upper bound, and leaves only the exact general-\(J\) constant and restricted score-only experiment transfer open.

sampling_model.design: There are fixed finite treated groups and a fixed finite menu of prespecified donor stacks with known weights. Each score is the treated-minus-donor contrast in baseline levels, pre-period slopes, and case-mix summaries. For adaptive inference, the first \(m_n\) iid observations in every primitive group form an independent pilot with \(m_n\to\infty\) and \(m_n/n\to0\); all remaining observations form the main sample.
sampling_model.units: At index \(n\), the observed law is \(\mathbb P_n=\bigotimes_{r\in\mathcal R}P_{r,n}^{\otimes n_r}\), with fixed \(R\), fixed \(J\), and stable positive group fractions. Disjoint pilot and main subsamples are independent because sampling is iid within every primitive group and groups are mutually independent.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is a fixed realized group-level assignment. Causal interpretation is conditional on consistency, a nonempty exact-zero donor set, and the shared-slope additive untreated-change restriction. These are substantive crux assumptions; sample ranking or near-balance does not imply them.
sampling_model.overlap: Every primitive group has a positive limiting sampling fraction. No treatment-propensity overlap condition is used. Weak separation concerns donor scores approaching the union of exact-zero faces, including faces with several zero labels.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Group means and centered within-group covariances are estimated directly. The known contrast matrix propagates all covariance caused by shared treated groups and reused controls, and eigenvalue clipping keeps every inverse totalized. The pilot uses only score means. Conditional on its retained label set, the untouched main sample calibrates the maximum of scalar score-residualized effect errors, including within-label outcome uncertainty; a singleton retained set therefore uses \(\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\).

prose_updates.related_work: RTI International documents a CMS comparison-state workflow based on ranked baseline distance, retention of two or three states, claims-driven substitutions, and person-level weighting; the reviewed source does not document ex ante algebraic equality to known administrative population totals. The exact-face results therefore supply a falsifiable abstract design analysis, not validation of the historical estimates. Conley--Taber and Ferman--Pinto use many controls to form reference distributions for few treated groups, unlike the present fixed labels with many within-group micro observations. Chernozhukov--Wuthrich--Zhu study cross-fitted and self-normalized synthetic-control average-effect inference under time-series asymptotics, not latent exact-zero donor faces. Berk et al. motivate simultaneous insurance and its multiplicity cost. Andrews--Kitagawa--McCloskey select an observed argmax option and target its attached mean; the present rule selects latent population-zero faces and targets their common ATT, so neither model contains the other without changing both selection and estimand. Their Proposition 3 motivates, but does not prove, the independent-pilot oracle-equivalence theorem. Evans--Hansen--Stark provide only a decision-dual template here because their theorem requires dominated product-measurable laws and minimizes expected size under a fixed sigma-finite measure, conditions not yet reduced to this expected-diameter problem. Andrews--Cheng, Andrews--Mikusheva, and Nussbaum motivate weak-limit and equivalence questions but do not provide the missing score-only transfer under the present assumptions.
prose_updates.interpretation: The causal target remains \(\tau_n\), defined from potential outcomes. A close donor identifies it only through the proved transport equation \(b_{j,n}-\tau_n=\beta_n^{\top}s_{j,n}\), not by definition. The finite-sample confidence sets are observed-law functionals of group means and covariances. Exact zero scores and the untreated-change model connect those functionals to the causal target; without either premise they are only comparison-state contrasts. The adaptive pilot changes the calibration constant, not the estimand or the identifying restriction.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The original full-vector Gaussian minimax risk is infinite when donor-effect spread is unrestricted, and a limit experiment with fixed Gaussian noise in \(b\) is incompatible with the root-\(n\)-consistent post-mean vector. The repaired local problem therefore observes \(b\) exactly, places Gaussian noise only on scaled scores, and bounds \(\max_j b_j-\min_j b_j\). The exact two-face Mahalanobis value and a finite simultaneous upper bound do not determine the exact general-\(J\), multiple-face constant. Evans--Hansen--Stark duality remains a proposed template until domination, product measurability, and a valid reduction from diameter to fixed-measure loss are established. Raw-data Le Cam equivalence is not claimed; only a restricted score-only reduced-experiment transfer could be pursued with additional QMD and uniform-integrability conditions. Local face coherence is an explicit Gaussian restriction unless a bounded-slope local subfamily is separately imposed; it does not follow from \(h_j=0\) alone.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Uniform coverage is conditional on the exact-close triangular-array class, including consistency, nonempty exact close sets, the almost-sure shared-slope additive untreated-change model, uniform fourth moments, covariance eigenvalue bounds, and stable group fractions. The original projected hull is only claimed to be root-\(n\) tight under fixed separation; it retains an all-\(J\) critical value. The independent-pilot hull is uniformly honest because selection is independent of main-sample calibration, and it is oracle-equivalent only under fixed separation with a unique close label. Multiple close labels are recovered as a face and calibrated jointly. Diagnostics may falsify calibration, placebo fit, omitted-predictor balance, or donor support, but cannot turn ranked sample near-balance into exact population equality. The bounded-spread score-only Gaussian frontier is finite and has an exact two-face subproblem; exact general-\(J\) optimality and restricted score-only transfer remain open. The historical CMS estimates are not validated by these conditional results.

statement_notes.justification: Honesty near label collisions remains useful only if the original projected hull is at least root-\(n\) tight when nonclose donors are fixed away from zero.
statement_notes.gap: The theorem removes false profiles and proves root-\(n\) diameter tightness, but its critical value still maximizes over all \(J\) labels; the separate pilot-adaptive theorem supplies oracle constants.
statement_notes.consumer: Applications may use this theorem for a rate guarantee, but should use thm:pilot-adaptive-oracle-equivalence rather than this result to claim ordinary one-label first-order endpoints.

proofs.proof_tex:
Choose distinct labels \(1,2\in\mathcal J\), which is possible because \(J\geq 2\), and choose a unit vector \(e\in\mathbb R^q\), which is possible because \(q\) is a positive integer.  Fix \(c\in(0,H]\).  Define two score configurations by
\[
h^{(0)}_1=0,\qquad h^{(0)}_j=ce\quad(j\neq 1),
\]
and
\[
h^{(1)}_2=0,\qquad h^{(1)}_j=ce\quad(j\neq 2).
\]
For each \(\Delta>0\), use the same effect vector in both configurations,
\[
b^{(\Delta)}_1=0,\qquad b^{(\Delta)}_2=\Delta,
\qquad b^{(\Delta)}_j=0\quad(j\geq 3).
\]
Each pair \((h^{(\ell)},b^{(\Delta)})\), \(\ell\in\{0,1\}\), belongs to \(\mathcal H_H\).  Indeed, every score norm is either zero or \(c\leq H\), and each configuration has exactly one zero-score label.  Consequently, the implication requiring equal \(b_j\)'s at two zero-score labels is vacuous.  By the definition of \(\tau(h,b)\), the two target values are
\[
\tau(h^{(0)},b^{(\Delta)})=0,
\qquad
\tau(h^{(1)},b^{(\Delta)})=\Delta.
\tag{1}
\]

Let \(m_{\ell,c,\Delta}\in\mathbb R^p\) be the interleaved mean vector of \(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}\) under \((h^{(\ell)},b^{(\Delta)})\), and put
\[
d_c=m_{1,c,\Delta}-m_{0,c,\Delta},
\qquad
\rho_c=\bigl(d_c^{\top}\Omega^{-1}d_c\bigr)^{1/2}.
\tag{2}
\]
Positive definiteness of \(\Omega\) guarantees that \(\Omega^{-1}\) and its positive-definite square root exist.  The effect coordinates cancel in \(d_c\); its first score block is \(ce\), its second score block is \(-ce\), and every other block is zero.  Thus \(d_c=c d_1\), with \(d_1\neq0\), and
\[
\rho_c=c\bigl(d_1^{\top}\Omega^{-1}d_1\bigr)^{1/2}\longrightarrow0
\qquad(c\downarrow0).
\tag{3}
\]
In particular, \(\rho_c\), and hence the distance between the two sampling laws, does not depend on \(\Delta\).

Write \(P_{\ell,c,\Delta}=N(m_{\ell,c,\Delta},\Omega)\).  Because \(\Omega\) is positive definite, both laws have everywhere-positive Lebesgue densities.  To calculate their total-variation distance, transform an observation \(z\) to
\[
x=\Omega^{-1/2}\left(z-\frac{m_{0,c,\Delta}+m_{1,c,\Delta}}{2}\right)
\]
and let \(u=\Omega^{-1/2}d_c/\rho_c\).  Then \(\|u\|_2=1\), the likelihood-ratio region on which the density under state \(1\) is at least that under state \(0\) is \(\{u^{\top}x\geq0\}\), and \(u^{\top}x\) has distribution \(N(-\rho_c/2,1)\) under state \(0\) and \(N(\rho_c/2,1)\) under state \(1\).  Integrating the density difference over that likelihood-ratio region therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\lVert P_{0,c,\Delta}-P_{1,c,\Delta}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
&=\Pr_{1,c,\Delta}(u^{\top}x\geq0)
  -\Pr_{0,c,\Delta}(u^{\top}x\geq0)\\
&=\Phi(\rho_c/2)-\Phi(-\rho_c/2)
=2\Phi(\rho_c/2)-1
=:v_c.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]

Now let \(K\) be any measurable confidence kernel satisfying the honesty constraint in the definition of \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)\).  Let \(Q_{\ell,c,\Delta}\) denote the joint law of \((Z^{\mathrm{pan}},C)\) obtained by first drawing \(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}\) from \(P_{\ell,c,\Delta}\) and then drawing the reported set \(C\) from \(K(Z^{\mathrm{pan}},\cdot)\).  Applying the same Markov kernel cannot increase total variation: for every measurable event \(A\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
|Q_{1,c,\Delta}(A)-Q_{0,c,\Delta}(A)|
&=\left|\int K(z,A_z)\,d(P_{1,c,\Delta}-P_{0,c,\Delta})(z)\right|\\
&\leq \lVert P_{1,c,\Delta}-P_{0,c,\Delta}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}=v_c,
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
where \(A_z=\{C:(z,C)\in A\}\) and \(0\leq K(z,A_z)\leq1\).  Define
\[
A_0=\{(z,C):0\in C\},
\qquad
A_1=\{(z,C):\Delta\in C\}.
\]
Membership of both parameter points in \(\mathcal H_H\), honesty, and (1) imply
\[
Q_{0,c,\Delta}(A_0)\geq1-\alpha,
\qquad
Q_{1,c,\Delta}(A_1)\geq1-\alpha.
\tag{6}
\]
Equations (5)--(6) and the union bound yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_{0,c,\Delta}(A_0\cap A_1)
&\geq Q_{0,c,\Delta}(A_0)+Q_{0,c,\Delta}(A_1)-1\\
&\geq (1-\alpha)+(1-\alpha-v_c)-1
=1-2\alpha-v_c.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
On \(A_0\cap A_1\), the reported set contains both \(0\) and \(\Delta\), so its diameter is at least \(\Delta\).  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{(h,b)\in\mathcal H_H}
\mathbb E_{h,b,\Omega}[\operatorname{diam}(K(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}))]
&\geq
\mathbb E_{h^{(0)},b^{(\Delta)},\Omega}[\operatorname{diam}(K(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}))]\\
&\geq \Delta\,Q_{0,c,\Delta}(A_0\cap A_1)\\
&\geq \Delta[1-2\alpha-v_c].
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
This proves the asserted two-face bound (and it is valid even when the displayed bracket is nonpositive).

Finally, (3), continuity of \(\Phi\), and \(\Phi(0)=1/2\) show that \(v_c\to0\) as \(c\downarrow0\).  Since \(0<\alpha<1/2\) and \(H>0\), there is \(c_0\in(0,H]\) such that \(\gamma_c:=1-2\alpha-v_c>0\) whenever \(0<c\leq c_0\).  Fix any such \(c\).  The effect vector is unrestricted in \(\mathcal H_H\), so (8) holds for every \(\Delta>0\) with the same positive constant \(\gamma_c\).  Letting \(\Delta\to\infty\) shows that the worst-case expected diameter of every honest \(K\) is infinite.  Taking the infimum over all honest kernels in the definition of \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)\) gives
\[
\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)=+\infty.
\]
Thus no honest procedure has finite worst-case expected diameter on the frozen face space, which proves the stated obstruction to a finite-valued or finitely attaining program.
